correctness.rationale: The update maps are q-contractions, and their exact interval images yield the three regimes. For q<1/2, the pair is affine and strongly separated, so the symmetric IFS law has no atoms and a Cantor support of the stated dimension. At q=1/2 the two half-interval similarities preserve the uniform distribution. For q>1/2 their image union is I and there is an interior flat segment f_+(J)=0; a uniform cylinder-diameter argument produces a fixed-length reset with probability at least 2^{-m} from every x∈I, yielding geometric TV convergence. Thus μ({0})>0 and finite-support distributions from 0 converge in TV; μ is concentrated on a countable dense orbit. At q≤1/2, finite-time measures from deterministic starts are mutually singular to the nonatomic invariant law. A standalone exact-rational verifier confirms 18 endpoint configurations and an explicit five-word global reset. Boundary hypotheses, TV normalization, limits and source scope have been checked independently of experiments.

originality.rationale: The core structural contribution is the exact common-atom Doeblin regeneration for overlapping two-point soft-threshold proximal updates and its sharp combination with a uniform and then separated Cantor law. Standard Hutchinson theory covers only the existence and separated affine-Cantor component. Compared proofs and hypotheses of Dai et al. (2023), Bianchi et al. (2017) and Sun et al. (2019); none inspected gives the stated trichotomy. The closest accessible published summaries concern deterministic composite trust-region step transitions, lasso ADMM finite support detection, noisy signSGD finite Markov chains, or generic affine quantum maps—not the same recurrence. Published searches do not certify priority; a general result about flat-spot random IFS could imply portions, so novelty is qualified.

value.rationale: The exact phase transition distinguishes stationary sparsity (a positive atom at the optimizer), dense support and strong mixing from continuous or Cantor stationary laws in the same elementary unbiased-noise proximal-gradient model. It reveals a genuine limitation of moment-based/weak-limit diagnostics of noisy sparse optimization and provides a constructive uniform regeneration bound, beyond a routine reparameterization or a table lookup. This is a full natural parameter classification for fixed-step scalar l1-regularized quadratic stochastic prox-gradient. The question is relevant to active-set identification and invariant distribution accuracy in persistent-noise algorithms, without implying general-dimensional performance.
